questionsApplications.label: How do digital technologies, generative AI and social-media algorithms reshape society, behaviour, beliefs and politics, and how can they be used responsibly?
How can digital and technological systems be designed and governed so that they are environmentally and socially sustainable?

alternatives.concept: A qualified interdisciplinary response combines digital-media analysis, AI ethics and the business and societal implications of AI with programming, data science, machine learning and algorithmic problem-solving. Sociology, politics, human rights and moral philosophy provide context for examining digital change. Quantitative and qualitative methods support inquiry; the regional sustainability project adds applied teamwork in another subject. These whole courses offer substantive tools and perspectives without reproducing Maastricht’s integrated digital-society theory, virtual-worlds work, critical making, dedicated digital politics and regulation, or 17 EC thesis.

Six advanced courses and whole7.5ECweights were reviewed. Poetry-led Creative Communication Laboratory is replaced with the actual AI search/optimisation course; no virtual-worlds, specialist digital-policy or thesis equivalence is claimed.

alternatives.concept: This related direction gives greater weight to the technical objects discussed by Digital Society: generative AI, algorithms and data analysis. Twelve courses in computing, mathematics, data science and AI provide technical depth. AI ethics, human rights, social-media analysis, misinformation, persuasion and behavioural decision-making add social and ethical perspectives. It does not reproduce the target’s humanities and social-science integration, dedicated digital regulation, virtual-worlds and critical-making sequence, or individual thesis. Technical depth alone is not claimed to reproduce the target degree.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has twelve courses in programming, computer science, AI, data science and mathematics (Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Networks & Operating Systems, Database Management Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures and Probability & Statistics), three on research methods and statistics (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Qualitative Research Methodology), and eight on the social, ethical and behavioural side (Ethics, Human Rights, Persuasive Communication, From T.V. to TikTok, Media Archaeology, Calling Bullshit, Marketing & Consumer Engagement and Behavioral Economics), plus Personal & Professional Development. The label names the technical majority first and the social and behavioural perspectives second; it does not claim a full computer-science or data-science degree.

basisLabels: Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Film & Media introduces the study of film and media, tracing the historical development of cinema and the elements of film form (narrative, cinematography, editing, sound) and treating media as cultural forms that reflect and shape society; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's media and digital-culture analysis by supplying the analytical vocabulary, although its main object is film rather than digital media. It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing”.

basisLabels: Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing
courseTraceability.rationale: Media Archaeology studies how pre-digital media technologies such as cassette tapes, typewriters and printed books shaped the production, circulation and preservation of knowledge, through material analysis and historical interpretation; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's history-of-ICT component (ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change) but addresses earlier media technologies rather than the digital revolution itself. It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital cultures, media and the history of ICT: Digital Cultures, Virtual Worlds and ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change, covering influencers, virtual worlds, emerging media and the historical development of computing”.

It implements the explicit academic basis “Digital technologies and critical making: Introduction to Digital Technologies I and II, Critical Making, the basics of coding and cyber security, and designing digital systems for social good”.

comparator.text: Elective space (30 EC): FASoS or UM minor, study abroad, internship, literature exam or approved electives
comparator.note: 30 EC open elective space, subject to the EER. Minors, IRO-managed study abroad, approved internship (12–24 EC), literature examination (up to 12 EC), or approved electives may contribute. External courses require prior approval and sufficient level without duplicated content. No optional route is instantiated.

notes.text: The alternatives offer substantive AI, data, media and social analysis through whole UCR courses. They do not reproduce the target’s integrated digital-society theory, dedicated digital politics and regulation, virtual-worlds work, critical making or individual thesis. General politics, rights, philosophy and sustainability remain contextual contributions.

Maastricht requires 120 EC in years one and two, followed by 30 EC of approved elective study, a 4 EC research experimentation component, 9 EC of controversies and a 17 EC thesis. Elective and progression conditions apply. UCR’s regional sustainability project does not replace the digital-society thesis. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Digital Society studies how digital technologies shape culture, politics, organisations and everyday life. It combines humanities and social-science analysis with digital skills, data, ethical inquiry and interdisciplinary research. The final year includes approved electives, research experimentation, controversies and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two qualified UCR alternatives offer related digital, social and ethical study. The first combines media and societal analysis with computing and AI; the second gives more weight to data, algorithms and technical AI. Their specialist content and research requirements differ from Maastricht’s integrated curriculum.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC includes 120 EC of compulsory first- and second-year study and 30 EC of approved electives, followed by research experimentation (4 EC), controversies (9 EC) and a thesis (17 EC). Progression, participation, registration and elective approval conditions apply. The optional third-year mentor scheme carries no credits.
